character_facts: Tonto becomes the life-support host for the infant by carrying him grafted onto his back.
The mother is shown acting in panic but also making the decisive choice that preserves the child.
Aghnar speaks as someone who sees himself as the continuing embodiment of the Metabarons and embraces mercilessness.
Oda-Honorata is addressed directly during the farewell and appears to oppose or answer Aghnar.
The infant is physically altered in infancy and is expected to grow into Steelhead, a future champion.
continuity_links: This page sets up the future figure called Steelhead.
It frames a coming confrontation between Aghnar and the grown child as fulfillment of clan tradition.
The final caption explicitly leads into the next episode, 'The Mentrek's solution'.
dialogue_meaning: The mother urgently seeks Tonto’s help to save the infant.
The narration explains the infant survives by being physically grafted onto Tonto’s back and sustained by Tonto’s circuits.
The child is being prepared for a later transformation involving a steel head.
Aghnar renounces peace, says the clan must live on, and commits himself to ruthless continuation of the Metabaron line.
Aghnar promises to return in the future to battle the grown child and destroy the steel head added to him.
Another character answers with a counter-vow that tradition will be fulfilled and that Steelhead will one day defeat Aghnar honorably.
locations: a surgical or biotech chamber filled with machinery and grafting equipment
a metallic hangar or launch bay
a departing spacecraft or long transport vessel
lore_facts: Advanced grafting technology can attach one living body to another in order to preserve life.
Tonto possesses 'zephyr circuits' or similarly named internal systems capable of keeping the infant alive.
A future rite or plan involves grafting a steel head onto the child once he reaches adult size.
The clan’s tradition appears to require a future duel between generations.
The title or name 'Steelhead' is tied to the child’s future identity and bodily transformation.
Honor, succession, and ritual combat are central values of the clan.
plot_events: A mother urgently carries a bio-infant to Tonto for help.
The infant’s body is grafted onto Tonto’s back so Tonto’s internal systems can keep the child alive.
The page states that when the child reaches adult size, a steel head will be grafted onto him.
A farewell is spoken to Oda-Honorata, along with a vow that the clan will continue.
Aghnar declares he will become the most merciless of the Metabarons and later return to fight the future warrior.
Another speaker invokes clan tradition and says Steelhead will become a champion and eventually triumph over Aghnar.
A ship or craft departs from the hangar, ending the scene on a departure cliffhanger.

visual_summary: A frantic woman runs through a machinery-filled medical space carrying a baby. In the next panel, the infant is shown being surgically grafted onto the back of a larger cyborg-like body amid cables and blood. A separate panel shows a blocky mechanical head or device associated with the infant’s future transformation. Below, two figures stand in a vast metallic hangar near a long dark vessel or platform; one figure appears mounted or fused to machinery. The scene ends with the craft departing through a large opening, and a caption announces the next episode.
